aboutParagraphs: Harrisons Tea Town is a tea and spices brand from Harrisons Malayalam Limited, a Kerala plantation company that describes more than 100 years of plantation experience. Its estates are in Munnar, Wayanad, and the Nilgiris. The brand sells online through harrisonsteatown.com and offers black, strong, masala, ginger, cardamom, lemon, tulsi lemon, green, mint green, white, organic, and detox teas, along with coffee, whole spice packs, bulk packs, and tea gift hampers. The company states that its teas are certified by Rainforest Alliance, Trustea, and the Ethical Tea Partnership.

Tea is a crowded category. A shopper scrolling through Instagram or the shelves of an online store sees dozens of brands, and most packs look similar. People choose based on what they drink, how the tea tastes, where it comes from, and whether they trust the name. For a brand with a plantation behind it, the story of where the leaf is grown is a real advantage, but it only helps when it is told clearly and without exaggeration.

This case study covers the social media work delivered by Teknoppy for the Tea Town brand: how the Instagram and Facebook presence is planned, what the campaign content is built around, and how it supports the online shop. It does not cover tea production, blending, pricing, or fulfilment, which belong to Harrisons Malayalam Limited.
challengeLead: Key challenges addressed during the social media engagement:

challenges.title: A wide range needed to feel easy to choose from
challenges.description: With more than a dozen tea types plus coffee and spices, a feed of random product shots leaves a new customer unsure where to start.

challenges.title: Plantation heritage had to be shown, not just stated
challenges.description: A century of plantation experience is a strong point. It needed to appear in content that a tea drinker can see and believe, not only as a line in a bio.

challenges.title: Tea drinkers have different reasons to buy
challenges.description: Someone buying strong tea for the family every month, someone trying green tea for a lighter routine, and someone choosing a gift hamper for a festival want different content.

challenges.title: A new venture competing with well-known names
challenges.description: Established tea brands already fill the shelves. A newer online brand needs a clear identity to be remembered after a few seconds of scrolling.

challenges.title: Social interest had to reach the shop
challenges.description: A follower who likes a post still needs a simple way to find that tea on the website and buy it.

objectiveLead: Teknoppy was engaged to plan and run social media campaign content that helps people discover, trust, and buy from Harrisons Tea Town. The brief centred on:
objectives: Presenting the tea range in clear groups so a new customer knows where to begin
Making the Harrisons Malayalam plantation background and certifications easy to notice
Building campaign content for festivals, gifting, and everyday tea routines
Keeping the brand name, product names, and tone consistent across Instagram, Facebook, and the website
Giving every profile and post a clear route to the online shop
approachLead: How Teknoppy built a structured social media presence around authentic buyer intent and plantation heritage:

approachPillars.title: Content grouped by how people drink tea
paragraphs: Posts are organised around the way customers think: strong tea for the daily cup, masala and ginger for a warming chai, green and white for a lighter routine, and lemon, tulsi, and detox blends for people who want something different. A visitor to the profile quickly sees which part of the range is for them.

approachPillars.title: The plantation story told simply
paragraphs: The tea comes from estates in Munnar, Wayanad, and the Nilgiris, operated by a company with over a century of plantation experience. That story is shared through content about the estates and the leaf, written plainly. Heritage works best when it is specific and calm.

approachPillars.title: Certifications used as proof
paragraphs: Rainforest Alliance, Trustea, and Ethical Tea Partnership certification are published by the company, and they appear in the content as reasons to trust the brand. Shoppers increasingly ask where their food comes from and how it is produced, so these details belong where a customer is deciding.

approachPillars.title: Campaigns for gifting and festive seasons
paragraphs: Tea and spice gift packs and hampers suit festivals and corporate gifting. Campaign content ahead of those periods shows the packs and explains what is inside, so a buyer planning gifts can choose without leaving the profile to search.

approachPillars.title: Instagram for the look, Facebook for the detail
paragraphs: Instagram carries the visuals: steam, leaf, cups, and pack shots. Facebook suits longer descriptions, brewing notes, and offers that reach a broader age group. Both platforms use the same names and details, so a customer who sees the brand in two places sees one consistent business.

approachPillars.title: Recipes and brewing, not only product shots
paragraphs: Content about how to make a good cup, which tea suits which time of day, and how to pair tea with food gives people a reason to follow. It also answers questions customers ask before they buy, such as which tea to try first.

approachPillars.title: One clear route to the shop
paragraphs: Profiles and posts point to the matching product or category on harrisonsteatown.com. A customer who has decided does not have to search for the tea they just saw.

approachPillars.title: Consistent naming across channels
paragraphs: The brand appears as Harrisons Tea Town, with the same product names, across Instagram, Facebook, and the website. This helps customers recognise one brand and helps search and AI tools connect the profiles, the site, and the parent company.

deliverables.description: Profiles managed with consistent brand name, tone, and links to the online shop.

deliverables.title: Range-based content themes
deliverables.description: Content planned around strong tea, masala and ginger, green and white, lemon, tulsi, and detox blends.

deliverables.title: Plantation and certification content
deliverables.description: The Harrisons Malayalam background and published certifications presented clearly.

deliverables.title: Festive and gifting campaigns
deliverables.description: Campaign content for tea and spice gift packs and hampers.

deliverables.title: Brewing and pairing content
deliverables.description: Posts that help customers choose and enjoy their tea, not only see it.

deliverables.title: A clear route to buy
deliverables.description: An obvious path from profile or post to the right product on harrisonsteatown.com.

whyMattersParagraphs: Food and drink brands are chosen on trust. A shopper cannot taste the tea through a screen, so they rely on what the brand shows and says: where it comes from, who stands behind it, and whether other people buy it. A profile that answers those questions clearly looks like an established brand. A profile that only posts product photos asks the customer to take a chance without giving them a reason.

The same clarity helps in search. Search engines and AI answer tools draw on social profiles, websites, and company information when someone asks which Kerala tea brand to try or where to buy plantation tea online. When the brand name, parent company, estates, and certifications are described the same way everywhere, those tools can represent Harrisons Tea Town accurately.

Social media works best alongside a brand's own website and product pages. Planned campaigns, rather than posts made only when there is news, keep the brand visible through the seasons when people buy tea and gifts, and they send readers on to the shop.

faqs.question: Who owns Harrisons Tea Town?
faqs.answer: Harrisons Tea Town is a venture of Harrisons Malayalam Limited, a Kerala plantation company based in Kochi.

faqs.question: Where is the tea grown?
faqs.answer: The company's estates are in Munnar, Wayanad, and the Nilgiris. Some spices are also grown on these estates.

faqs.question: What types of tea does Harrisons Tea Town sell?
faqs.answer: The range includes black, strong, masala, ginger, cardamom, lemon, tulsi lemon, green, mint green, white, organic, and detox teas, along with coffee, whole spices, bulk packs, and gift hampers.

faqs.question: Is the tea certified?
faqs.answer: The company states that its teas are certified by Rainforest Alliance, Trustea, and the Ethical Tea Partnership.

faqs.question: Can I buy Harrisons Tea Town online?
faqs.answer: Yes. The tea is sold on harrisonsteatown.com, with shipping and shipment tracking pages on the site. Check the site for current delivery details and shipping offers.

faqs.question: Is there a gift option for festivals or corporate orders?
faqs.answer: Yes. The brand offers tea gifts, gift hampers, and whole spice packs for festive and corporate gifting, and it lists customised tea and spice options on its website.

faqs.question: Can I visit a plantation or stay on an estate?
faqs.answer: Harrisons Malayalam Limited runs Tea Town Kerala, a tea tourism division offering plantation holidays in Munnar and Wayanad. It is based on Bristow Road, Willingdon Island, Kochi.

faqs.question: Which social media pages does Harrisons Tea Town run?
faqs.answer: The brand is on Instagram as @harrisons.teatown and on Facebook, with the same name and product details on both.

faqs.question: Does Teknoppy manage social media for food and beverage brands?
faqs.answer: Yes. Teknoppy plans and manages Instagram and Facebook campaigns for food, beverage, and hospitality brands, with content built around the questions customers ask before they buy.
